That's not accurate, at least not according to current data — the US has not been added to Vietnam's visa-free list. US passport holders still do NOT have visa-free access to Vietnam; there's no bilateral or unilateral exemption for American citizens.

What you'll need instead:
- **E-Visa** (recommended pathway for US citizens): up to 90 days, cost is USD 25 for single-entry or USD 50 for multiple-entry, processing takes about 2-3 business days (faster options available for a higher fee). You can apply at https://evisa.gov.vn/. It's valid for entry by air, land, or sea, and e-Visas are available to all nationalities.
- Make sure your passport is valid for at least 180 days from your date of entry.

The 45-day visa-free perk you may be thinking of applies to a separate list of countries (mostly European nations plus a few others) that Vietnam has unilaterally exempted — the US isn't on it.

This is based on policy data as of 2026-08-17, so I'd recommend double-checking at evisa.gov.vn before you book, in case anything's changed since.
